samples.marker_line: Zombie/Cosmu infector: detect backup deletion and small packed builds
reverse_engineering: Unicorn emulation maps the PE, stack and synthetic Windows API stubs. It stops at the packer handoff 0x407bab; recovered original entry is 0x402130. No specimen filesystem or networking APIs execute on the host.
Original main calls GetLogicalDrives at 0x40202a, constructs drive-letter roots, and calls recursive traversal 0x401cf0. File selection 0x401ba0 routes EXE/exe candidates into 0x401340.

Joiner 0x401340 reads its own module path, writes its image and the original host to a temporary file via fgetc/fputc loops, records 0x38-byte metadata and an 8-byte footer, deletes the victim path at 0x401684, and renames the joined temporary file at 0x401748. Host replay logic reads the footer at 0x401f82 and reconstructs/launches the original host.
Suffix comparisons at 0x401c23/0x401c36/0x401c49/0x401c5c identify Ghost-image and BAK backups and all jump to DeleteFileA at 0x401c80. This is a separate destructive branch, not an exclusion list.
The original bytes retain the Zombie.exe working-copy path and GBK host-recovery message. The family rule missed them solely because 40686 bytes is below the former 60000-byte floor.
Self-deletion helper 0x401040 obtains the current module path, converts it to 8.3, constructs COMSPEC /c del with nul redirection, and invokes ShellExecuteExA.

samples.marker_line: StormAttack installer: describe DNS banner without inferring flooding
reverse_engineering: PE CRT entry 0x402674 reaches dispatcher 0x401cb0. Configuration dword 0x404120 equals 3: this selects 0x401900 at 0x401f8a, followed by self-deletion helper 0x401390.
0x401900 constructs an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key, sets StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads and patches its own image, writes a new copy and starts it at 0x401b7e.

Alternate installer routine 0x401260 opens LanmanServer Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL at 0x401320 and replaces it with the System32 DLL path at 0x40133e. Resource extraction and WriteFile stage resource 101; 0x401150 starts a host process and passes a resolved LoadLibraryA address and remotely written DLL path into CreateRemoteThread.
0x401390 resolves its own short path and COMSPEC, builds /c del > nul, starts the command suspended, then resumes it. This code supports the cleanup objective independent of family labels.

Embedded PE at file offset 0x5060 identifies a StormAttack DNS-labeled module through its banner pair and STORM command format. Its code region is zero-filled and the entry maps to zeros. Family identity is retained; successful loading, packet control, direct flooding or reflection are not established.
No Remcos or WannaCry implementation was established. Collection filenames and sandbox scores were not treated as behavior.

samples.identification: Mirai-derived ARM EABI native bot and propagation loader
samples.marker_line: Mirai ARM bot: correct loader hostname marker attribution
reverse_engineering: ARM main 0x11cd0 initializes its runtime, detaches and starts the propagation child via 0x15f1c. The child calls state machine 0x142bc at 0x15f50.

The target-session state machine handles credential/login failure responses and sends shell enable commands, then recognizes BusyBox output. At 0x14b18 it selects chmod +x .d; ./.d; ./dvrHelper selfrep and sends it at 0x14b28.

Send wrapper 0x19434 reaches 0x193f0, which loads syscall 289 and issues SVC 0 at 0x193f8 (ARM send). This binds propagation strings to remote-session effects rather than treating their presence as proof.

0x15858..0x15928 sends wget/TFTP/ftpget/curl command fragments, interleaves the configured server address and pipes downloaded shell scripts into sh. 0x14e90 sends the BusyBox hostname PBOC marker through the same wrapper; that reference is loader behavior, not evidence of a process killer.

0x10590 reads /proc/net/tcp and inspects /proc process executable/fd information; GET/dlr. is used by the loader search path. These observations support the existing procfs/loader identity alongside executable propagation.

RC4 implementation 0x160c0 initializes a 256-byte permutation, swaps entries in its key schedule, then derives S[(S[i]+S[j]) & 255] and XORs bytes into the destination at 0x16238..0x16270. Wrapper 0x16290 calls the transform for encoded configuration buffers. The notable RC4 trait accurately identifies implementation presence.

HTTP and JSON-looking literals participate in the random-padding generator 0x123ec: it selects a template then adds random characters, called by framing helper 0x124fc. Generic HTTP/2 preface and header detections describe literal protocol content; they do not establish actual HTTP/2 transport or exfiltration.

trait_changes: Require native suffix-dispatch code in the packed drive-joiner objective; an inert reference table is insufficient.
Add the generalizable drive-wide BAK/Ghost backup-deletion objective in impact/destroy/file-deletion, with a notable selection primitive in fs/search.
Lower Zombie family size floor to 16 KiB; retain semantic family and infection evidence.
Rename killer-pboc-hostname-marker to loader-pboc-hostname-command at notable; preserve its matcher and scope. No YAML consumers referenced the old ID.
Describe StormAttack DNS identity text as a DNS-labeled banner; preserve identity matchers and severity.

verification.initial_and_final_scans: atomscan --no-update --follow=none --mode slow -f json on every full sample path
verification.facts: cleave facts on each original sample; raw and decoded text, imports, sections and metrics reviewed
verification.controls: original, rebased operands, changed branch, absent backup table, absent DeleteFileA name, absent family labels, inert RET-entry PE with all reference-table legs
verification.external_reports: Supplied Triage and MalwareBazaar URLs were inaccessible; verdicts use specimen bytes and traced code, not external scores.
verification.safety: No specimens were run natively. Only the first PE packer was CPU-emulated with synthetic APIs; no sample-directed network requests were made.
